open_problems.OP-26: Proved scaled displacement estimate for the line in bounded slow time. Gauge-corrected 0.02-site criterion and independent verification remain open. A uniform norm estimate near the band edge gives a forced Schrodinger envelope and semiclassical position concentration. It does not certify the connection-corrected full-period criterion.
open_problems.OP-28: Conditional realization with bounded scalar signs and growing sheet order. Fixed bounded scalar roots obstruct the exact uniform phase law. General bounded-resource encodings unresolved.
open_problems.OP-29: Three-step full site/channel records conditionally prepare the holonomy plane from a localized sheet. Positive-time record effects on even rings miss every cross-parity coherence. Physical selection of the instrument, same-parity tomography, phase reference and band preparation remain open. Finite native branches cannot isolate a single faithful real plane when phi(M)>2. On five sheets, the destructive-constructive filter attains the minimum leakage at its integer squared count whenever the constant sector is absent.
open_problems.OP-18: On the prepared nontrivial real holonomy plane the step and sheet-unresolved vertex projectors generate a complex matrix algebra, with central complex structure unique up to sign. This leaves effect access and physical correspondence open.
open_problems.OP-22: One shared sheet gives complex tensor dynamics, with an explicit optional entangling contact shift. Independent sheets retain relative orientation sectors. Selection of a shared sheet and physical interaction, and an interacting classical limit remain open.
open_problems.OP-21: Flag marginals, rotation invariance and product odds classify weights on the full field as real embeddings. Native localized-sheet records cannot distinguish embeddings that fix the coin. Uniform ordering, regularity or an independently calibrated extension remains open. Native localized protocols have rational finite branch weights and identical full transcript laws for every embedding. A repeated filter selects the larger quadratic root as an operational limit; identifying it with a separately named root remains open.
open_problems.OP-27: Local balanced mixing implies the parallelogram identity under the flagged preparation and endpoint-weight assumptions. It leaves the record law and apparatus to be grounded. Z5 G10 derives a restriction by continuation under a different history-event assumption.

gates.current_evidence: The lift stipulates a line or ring, binary signed mixing and M cyclic sheets. A localized-sheet state and sector states give different three-step records on the same graph.
gates.remaining: Specify a primitive or discriminator that selects the carrier.
gates.name: Primitive selection
gates.baseline_evidence: Finite relational structures, signed graphs and gain graphs are available as primitives; none is selected. A directed three-cycle supports both a complex-type algebra and a classical simplex (Director A, A2). Transport on a graph takes arbitrary values in arbitrary groups (G7-01-01). Edition Z3: a requirement restricts the primitive: consistency of the pair measure under continuation admits, with trivial gains, permutations only; on undirected gain graphs, involutions only; for out-degree two and unit gains, arc digraphs of 2-in 2-out digraphs with a sign -1 (G9-01-02 to G9-01-04). The requirement is supplied. Rectagraphs carry a transport of their own, trivial exactly on Cayley graphs of elementary abelian 2-groups (G9-01-11).

gates.current_evidence: A record is the measured site and channel with sheets unresolved. The same apparatus with an additional coherent sector preparation changes the outcome law. Three-step site/channel records give two informative outcomes and four single-path outcomes. Observing every single step makes sector information inaccessible. The optional independently timed local coin and freely prepared flagged rows are additional operational inputs.
gates.remaining: Derive the available preparations, record algebra and their equivalences from primitives.
gates.name: Operational event structure
gates.baseline_evidence: Unrestricted contextual tables do not select the quantum subset (TO-0). GH-1 uses walk sets as events with end vertices as records; the record role is supplied (G8). Edition Z3: with the distinction between returning and non-returning walks admitted, an additive weighting of returning walks by a class function of their holonomy exists (G8-01-01, revised; Directors A, B, G). What counts as a record decides which orders of rule can see the transport.

gates.current_evidence: A complex two-channel Fourier fibre, including a pure-band preparation, is stipulated. Real conjugate sectors form a real plane. Given coherent controlled shifts, balanced mixing and postselection, the explicit filter K concentrates a prepared dipole on the selected real plane. Native three-step blocks perform conditional plane preparation without auxiliary coherent routing. Individual-phase, parity and readout restrictions limit attainable effects. Finite native branch support is closed under the cyclotomic conjugates of a fixed order. At M=5 a three-step filter saturates the derived leakage bound for its sheet counts.
gates.remaining: Derive access to the projective instrument, identify achievable same-parity effects, and prepare a base band after a successful sheet record.
gates.name: State and effect spaces
gates.baseline_evidence: Pure-state geometry does not fix the mixed-state theory: classical spin on S^2 (Directors A, G). GH-1 gives a Hilbert space by the Dowker-Johnston-Sorkin construction, conditional (G8-01-05). Edition Z3: the cubic Veronese model has the qubit table on a designated family of pure tests and a ten-dimensional state space (Director G); with those tests only it is the qubit, with all affine effects pure states at Bloch angle 60 degrees are perfectly distinguishable (G7 Section 5). Which tests are admitted is a separate obligation (OP-29).

gates.current_evidence: The cyclic cover has an exactly computable permutation monodromy. The odd-cycle elementary path difference determines a real spectral pair after the fibre and diamonds are designated.
gates.remaining: Identify transition geometry independently of the chosen sheet representation.
gates.name: Transition geometry
gates.baseline_evidence: Finite homogeneous carriers excluded (G7-01-07, G7-01-09; Gelander 2013). Curvature 1 against 4 separates RP^2 from the qubit (Directors A, G; G7 Remark 5.2). Inhomogeneous nets exist with imported geometry (Directors A, B). Dense inhomogeneous subsets from gain graphs, conditional (G8-01-05). Algebraic generating data fix p only up to field automorphisms (G7-01-13). Edition Z3: the growth condition holds exactly when the closed walks of even length realize every group element; the type of the limit space follows the group they realize (G8-01-10; witnesses of Directors A, B, G).

gates.current_evidence: Conjugate sectors give opposite field angles. Opposite orientations have the same minimal holonomy eigenvalue. No internal orientation or physical complex structure is selected. Real step and sheet-unresolved record projectors on the selected plane generate M_d(C). Their real commutant is C. A real preparation and full record leave the two absolute orientations indistinguishable.
gates.remaining: Identify a physical phase reference and the accessible effects under native operations, including the need for cross-parity measurements.
gates.name: Phase and complex structure
gates.baseline_evidence: Transition probabilities fix all Bargmann phases up to one conjugation, constructively (G7-01-10, G7-01-11); three overlaps alone do not (Directors A, G; Li-Wagner-Zhang 2026); the determinant of one loop does not (Director B, B2). Global conjugation of a whole model is unobservable (Director B, B2); relative orientation is fixed by composition (G7-01-15). Complex structure, symplectic form, dynamical correspondence and equality of generator and observable counts are forms of one postulate (G7-01-06, G7-01-12). Edition Z3: a real reversible step has a complex structure of its own, unique under a positive generator and reversed with the step (G9-01-05; Stueckelberg 1960; Moretti-Oppio 2017 for Poincare symmetry); the vertex records do not commute with it and the commutant of step and records is real (G9-01-06). On signed Cayley rectagraphs the class matrices have a central complex structure exactly for k = 3 mod 4, with k supplied (G9-01-12). No warrant for complex amplitudes.

gates.current_evidence: The three-step record is (1+cos(2h))/4 under the squared-norm rule. Tracing a localized sheet yields 1/4 for M>2. The supplied Born instrument yields an exact mixture of finite categorical laws. Bayesian sector inference uses this rule as a premise. With flagged rows, remote marginal independence and holonomy invariance, local boundedness in the decoded plane selects its squared norm. Without topology, product statistics on the full exact number field select any one real embedding. Native records on a localized sheet cannot identify the embedding when it fixes the real coin. The native observed field is Q. Adaptive sheet-resolved experiments, independent copies and stopping have zero total variation between embedding laws. An ordered conditional-frequency limit selects an operational class.
gates.remaining: Identify a primitive that warrants an embedding-sensitive preparation, instrument or order, or give a complete empirically grounded formulation on equivalence classes.
gates.name: Probability rule
gates.baseline_evidence: Squared-norm rule from invariance, second order and strong positivity on a gain graph (G8-01-02, G8-01-03). Second order is supplied. No third-order interference alone does not select quantum theory (Directors A, B, G; Barnum-Mueller-Ududec 2014). Edition Z3: the measures at successive lengths are not related by continuation in general (Directors A, B); the same carrier supports a classical Markov walk and an additive holonomy weighting (Director A); the representation-free pair measure is the coincidence count on the cover (G8-01-09).

gates.current_evidence: The base and sheet tensor factors enter the construction by definition. They do not derive independent physical systems, entanglement, instruments or an interaction law. The ordinary real tensor product carries two relative orientations invisible to product measurements. A common sheet realizes the complex product. A collision-dependent sheet shift entangles a product preparation; its one-step weak-field strength tends to zero at fixed coupling. Every algebraic local unitary and complete algebraic instrument preserves spectator marginals after applying the same field embedding globally. Independent product probabilities exclude generic convex mixtures of embeddings.
gates.remaining: Derive a shared reference or its equivalent from independent preparations; establish admissible joint measurement and interaction laws.
gates.name: Composition
gates.baseline_evidence: Single-system data do not fix the composite: minimal against quantum (Director B; G7-01-14); interpolated family K_t and failure of its uniform four-system extension by t(1-t)/4 (Director G); CNOT closure forces the quantum composite once a complex representation is given (Director G). Product of gain graphs gives the full tensor product with a common step count (G8-01-06). Edition Z3: the interpolated composites are not closed under selective local filters, no four-party weight repairs them, a matching hierarchy is closed under weaker operations and excludes GHZ, one pure entangled seed with local filters gives all states (Directors A, B; recomputed); the product of gain graphs is a tensor product at each length and can be smaller over all lengths (Director G).

gates.current_evidence: The signed orthogonal step on the lift restricts exactly to the electric walk. A separate low-band, zero-field limit obeys a controlled free Schrödinger envelope equation. The real shared-sheet update reduces exactly to a tensor walk, with an optional contact phase. With h=F eps delta^3 a low-band section converges in spinor norm to the constant-force Schrodinger envelope on a common scaling family.
gates.remaining: Derive the allowed dynamics, clock and physical parameters, with general forces and interacting systems.
gates.name: Dynamics
gates.baseline_evidence: Static geometry does not select a generator or clock (Director A). Walk length on a gain graph is not unitary (G8 Section 9). No calibrated time. Edition Z3: a step consistent under continuation is unitary up to a factor (G9-01-01); for the signed arc digraph of a ring it has two branches of opposite group velocity (G9-01-07). The requirement and the carrier are supplied; the generator is a choice of logarithm. exp(-isH) on an undirected gain graph is a formal completion with imported imaginary unit and parameter (Director G).

gates.current_evidence: Position, sheet adjacency, ordering of updates and the rescaled time are supplied. A square path comparison defines an exact discrete transport.
gates.remaining: Derive distance, clock units, causality and a justified relation to a spacetime connection.
gates.name: Space, causal and clock structure
gates.baseline_evidence: Ehlers-Pirani-Schild template only (Director D). No construction. Edition Z3: in GH-2 the clock is the step count without unit and the ring is supplied (G9 Section 8).

gates.current_evidence: For a prepared single band of the line walk, the scaled mean displacement follows a classical Hamiltonian ray ensemble over bounded slow time with the proved error bound (1). For shrinking-action packets with delta^2/eps tending to zero, the scaled lattice position law converges weakly to the Newtonian point Y0+p0 t-F t^2/2 on bounded times.
gates.remaining: Prepare the assumed wave packet after filtering, control position distributions, and derive an interacting Hamiltonian limit in calibrated variables.
gates.name: Classical Hamiltonian mechanics
gates.baseline_evidence: Dephasing gives a stochastic channel, not a Hamiltonian flow (FAR-1; Director A). Recorded walks give the counting measure (G8-01-07). Classical and quantum pure states share a Poisson description (Landsman 1997). No derivation. Edition Z3: in GH-2 position over steps has the distribution of the group velocity (quoted, Grimmett-Janson-Scudo), a linear gain translates the quasi-momentum exactly (G9-01-09), and packets follow the rays of w(k) + Phi x over one period in instances (deviation 0.61 to 0.65 site; no error bound). One walk, one dimension, linear potential only. A staircase of order-4 gains does not follow the ray of its mean field.

gates.current_evidence: The explicit weak-field centroid and free-envelope estimates use different scalings. Bounded scalar signs coexist with unbounded sheet count and holonomy order. Ideal odd-cycle dipole-filter success is asymptotically 4 pi^2/M^3. A shift-only Kraus operator with supplied coherent routing needs 1,202 consecutive successful applications in the M=63 example under the stated tolerance bound. Native records have explicit preparation and classification costs. At M=63, 6,464 informative records give a uniform 1% classification-error bound under the stipulated law. The forced-envelope norm bound displays separate frame, dispersion and integration errors; eps=delta gives an explicit diagonal sequence with the same constant-force Hamiltonian. With C the integer squared sheet count at a recorded vertex on five sheets and zero constant component, the smaller faithful-plane weight e satisfies e(1-e)>=4/(5*C^2).
gates.remaining: Prove the required preparation and observation costs and a general interacting limit with physical units.
gates.name: Quantitative limit
gates.baseline_evidence: Exact homogeneity excluded; three forms of limit remain; ordering of values has to be supplied for algebraic data (G7-01-13, G8-01-08). Edition Z3: growth criterion proved (G8-01-10). A weak force was obtained only with gains of growing order, for which the measure depends on the character (G8-01-08; OP-28).

gates.current_evidence: The proposed three-step record discriminates stipulated preparations. The existing atomic quantum-walk experiment supplies an externally grounded implementation of an assumed law. An independent external tag would distinguish two five-sheet weights. A localized-sheet native experiment gives identical probabilities in both. The forced packet uses dimensionless coordinates without an external calibration.
gates.remaining: Identify primitive-linked preparation, units, observable and uncertainty yielding a distinctive physical prediction.
gates.name: Empirical correspondence

gates.current_evidence: Neither of the two limits derives the quantum and classical packages from the same independently warranted primitives, with an empirical map. Original target remains unresolved. Conditional access to a complex algebra and an interacting product example are established separately from physical gate passage. The uniform-force quantum and classical limits now share one scaling family and premise set within a restricted toy model.
